newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady, testing trend line support.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady, testing trend line support.

text.p: June Brent crude futures in Asia were steady at midday on Tuesday, looking to test trend line support.
June was quoted at $17.80/$18.05 per barrel, around the London close on Friday of $17.97. London's IPE and SIMEX Brent were closed on Monday to mark a U.K. holiday.
NYMEX crude on ACCESS was steady in Asian trading.
June was last traded at $19.65, up two cents from New York overnight, which closed up three cents at $19.63.
A broker said June Brent short-term trend-line support was at $17.97 and needed to trade above that level to resume a test of the upper end of the trading range of $17.50 to $18.77.
However, a failure to hold above $17.97 would allow prices to slide to at least $17.80, he said.
New York prices rose in early dealings on Monday by worries that ethnic clashes in Nigeria would disrupt crude supplies.

Oil Minister Dan Etete was quoted in a Nigerian newspaper as saying a 125,000 barrels-per-day refinery was shut down following clashes. If it was not reopened soon it could create fuel shortages, he was quoted saying.
